annotations.text:
The shared core is Ryder Carroll's rapid-logging grammar:
• task   x done   > migrated   < scheduled
○ event   – note   * priority

It's plain text, so one parser in Rails can serve the TUI, the web app, and even piped stdin.

Architecture sketch: Rails is the system of record — a Hotwire/Turbo PWA for the phone, plus a JSON API. The TUI is a small Ruby client of that same API, with a local SQLite cache so rapid logging works offline and syncs later.
Migration is the soul of the method, so both clients treat it as a deliberate ritual — a wizard in the TUI, cards on the phone. Nothing auto-rolls over; the friction is the feature.

Open questions for v0.1:
– offline conflict rules (last-write-wins per entry?)
– auth for the TUI (device token vs. OAuth)
– custom collections: structured entries or free-form pages?
– is the dark 'terminal-kin' alt worth losing the paper feel? (It gains one look everywhere, but the analog warmth is what drew you to BuJo.)
